doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Tonight Show ends with Carson's departure and what came after
summary: Young says the band left the night Carson did his last show, he was ready with work including the Clayton-Hamilton band, and he did a couple later shows with the new band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: So when the Tonight Show Band, when Johnny left then the band ended, then that was the end of, when Johnny Carson left the Tonight Show that was it.

You know, when Johnny Carson left the Tonight Show that was the last night for Doc Severinsen and the Tonight Show band. We left the same night. We didn‘t play the next day, or anything. When Johnny Carson did his last show, Tonight Show did it‘s last show because Johnny and Doc and Ed McMahon was a three, they had a… they had a thing and we knew it, the band knew that that was it. They just said, ―Sure is a drag to have to give up a gig like that,‖ but that night, that was it, never did another Tonight Show. They called me back to do a couple, for some trumpet players who wasn‘t there, but it was with the new group that was there, and I didn‘t want to, I did it, but I just went on in and, make the bread, you know what I‘m saying. I didn‘t want to play with that new age band and everything.
Did you have enough advanced notice?
Did I have what?
Advanced notice that the band was going to end?
Oh yeah, we knew, we knew that was the last night when Johnny left, we knew that the Tonight Show band was leaving and we left right then.
Were you prepared for that? Did you set up other kinds of work so that you didn‘t, so when you left the band you had some work?
Oh yeah, back then there was a lot of work in town and different places and different things, in fact I was with the band I‘m with right now.
Yeah, started getting popular and moving and different things. And so I did… Jeff…
The Clayton-Hamilton band?
Clayton-Hamilton band, and then we started doing different things. And so, most of the musicians were busy anyway. You know what I‘m saying?
Got you.
Some of the musicians, all the musicians weren‘t, but some of the musicians were busy doing other things and so when you left there, it didn‘t bother you, financially it didn‘t bother you.
So, you were ok.
Huh?
You were ok.
Yeah, I was ok.
Okay.

Yeah, I was okay I started playing with, and we were doing a lot of studio work, recordings and different things, and a lot of things was happening, and that‘s not happening now, I think it might be happening, but the other musicians are taking over, you know the younger guys or what have you, because we were all busy, man.
